newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Profit-taking stalls Taiwan stock bull run at end.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking stalls Taiwan stock bull run at end.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished slightly lower on Tuesday as profit-takers cashed in on the market's dramatic November rise of more than 300 points, but brokers said the bulls had yet to run their course.
The weighted index finished 11.10 points or a scant 0.16 percent lower at 6,927.77. Turnover was a hectic T$104.37 billion, down from Monday's five-month-high T$115.29 billion.
"Many investors decided to slow their pace after the big recent gains," said Foremost Investment analyst Norman Lee.
Institutional selling also added to the general mood of post-rise caution, brokers said.
The conclusion of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum had little impact on local market, brokers said.
"The market did not react to APEC's conclusion because there was no surprise announcement," Lee said.

Asset-backed and food shares rose to support the market, while recent star sectors, such as plastics and electronics, encountered profit-taking against sharply higher prices that had added well over 300 points to the index in November.
Taiwan Tea Corp gained T$4 or 5.84 percent to T$72.5.
Computer giant Acer Inc fell T$1.5 or 2.78 percent to T$52.5 and Mitac was down 90 cents or 2.77 percent to T$31.5.
Brokers said the 7,000-point level posed a key technical and psychological resistance in the near term.
"It may take a few days of consolidation before the market feels confident enough to challenge 7,000 points," said Alex Yang, an analyst at National Securities.
"But overall the market is still bullish," Yang said.
A range of 6,900-7,000 was seen for Wednesday.
